# Game show — Style Prompt

> A rhythm-game variety show in flat vector: toy-like mascots with thick ink outlines hop on candy-coloured sets (a rotating sunburst, scrolling stripes, polka dots), every pop, drop, stamp, bite and camera punch lands on one fast tempo grid, a round card opens each round, the round is one verb repeated on the beat that speeds up, and a big outlined judgement word closes it. White telops with a thick ink stroke carry all the words.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

- **Everything is on the grid.** One fixed, fast tempo (the reference runs 150 BPM: a beat is 0.4 s, a bar 1.6 s). Every event sits at a (bar, beat) or a clean subdivision of it: cuts on bar lines, drops on quarter beats, bites on beats, then on half beats, typed characters on sixteenths. The film is silent here, so the grid is what you see: hops, squashes and punches pulse with it.
- **One drawing kit, many sets.** Flat fills, one heavy ink outline with round caps and joins, hard offset shadows. Each round gets a new saturated set: one background hue plus the same hue one step lighter as a pattern.
- **Characters are toys.** One bean-shaped body for the whole cast, told apart by body colour, a belly patch, one head accessory and a name tag. They hop on the beat, squash when they land or get hit, throw both arms up on a shout.
- **A round = a repeatable verb + a win.** Split the topic into rounds. Each round has one action that can repeat on a beat (bite, stamp, stack, answer, hammer) and ends on a judgement the audience reads at a glance.

Not a minigame frenzy (no timers, no new art style per round), not a mid-century cartoon (no painted textures, no character acting), not a stage talk (no slow fades, no gradients, no soft shadows), not 3D.

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Vector only** at 1920×1080: flat fills, one near-black ink, 8 px outlines on characters and props, 5-7 px on small parts (antenna tips, flags, mittens), round joins and caps.
- **No gradients, blur, texture or soft shadows.** Depth is a hard offset shadow: the same shape in ink shifted 10 px (banners, slots) to 14 px (cards) down-right, the coloured shape on top.
- **Sets**: one saturated ground plus a pattern one step lighter: a sunburst of 14 rays (each 12.9° wide, 28 slices) rotating about the frame centre, diagonal stripes (50-70 px wide, leaning −20° to −25°, sometimes scrolling), offset polka dots (r 12 px every 90 px, alternate rows shifted half a step, 25 % white). A darker floor band with an 8 px ink line on top grounds a playing scene (top at y 880, feet stand at y 930).
- **Characters** (bean units, foot at 0,0, height 172): a rounded bean body, stubby arms (28 × 70, rx 14) with white mitten hands (r 17), two foot ellipses, oval eyes (11 × 16) with a white catch-light, pink cheeks, a curved mouth that swaps to an open one with a red tongue, a lighter belly ellipse. One accessory on top: an antenna with a ball, heart, question mark, bolt, moon, cloud, sprout or star; or a beret, captain's cap, black cap, red-and-white headband, mustache, long ears. Crowd scale 0.55 (back row) and 0.68 (front row); a playing contestant about 1.2.
- **Props** are built from the same kit: a wooden frame with a dark beam, a wavy-edged cracker on a string (a bite is a round hole with an ink arc on its edge), cards, pills, stamps.
- **UI kit**: round card (cream, 10 px outline, radius 50, 14 px shadow, a coloured tag pill on its top edge), corner banner (top-left, radius 24, 7 px outline, 10 px shadow), judgement word, burst (8-point star + white ring + 8 speed lines), name-tag pills (ink pill with a white rim), stamp (double red border).

## 3. Colour logic

- `--latar` is the opening stage set: the sunburst ground. Its rays are `--latar` mixed 66/34 with `--latar-2` (a lighter step of the same hue) plus 12 % `--utama`, so a white brand still shows its sunburst; its dots 25 % white.
- `--latar-2` is every card and paper surface: the round card, the registration or report card. Text on it is `--teks` (ink) and `--utama-di-latar` for the one coloured line (a time, a contact).
- `--utama` is the round: the round card's set (stripes of `--utama` 82 % with white) and its tag pill, with the tag's telop in `--teks-di-utama` over an ink stroke. The playing set is `--utama` mixed 64 % with `--latar-2`, its stripes 76 %, its floor `--utama` 85 % with ink.
- `--aksen` is the corner banner (telop and sub line in `--teks-di-aksen`) and the finale set (rays 84 % `--aksen` with white, floor 78 % with ink).
- **One set = one hue**, and neighbouring rounds never share one: the brand's background, main colour, a tint of it, then the accent. More rounds take tints and mixes of these, never a new unrelated hue.
- **Fixed in every brand**: ink `#1b1b1b` (all outlines, hard shadows, name-tag pills, hole marks), white (telop fill for big words, mittens, catch-lights), the count-in red `#ff5a5f` (also the stamp and the red of the flags), the judgement pink `#ff8fb1`, burst yellow `#ffd23f`, wood `#c98a52` / `#8e5530`, cracker cream, and the cast's fifteen body colours (`#3aa0ff`, `#7b5cff`, `#ff7a1a`, `#dadde8`, `#4b505c`, `#8ed1fc`, `#ffb84d`, `#ff6fa8`, `#f4e9d8`, `#4e7cf6`, `#19b388`, `#d97757`, `#4d6bfe`, `#6c8cff`, `#a7afc2`). A contestant's colour is its identity and never changes; never stand a character on a set of its own hue.
- Big words on a set are white telops with an ink stroke, so they read on a pale brand (as outlined letters) and on a dark one (as white letters).

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul` carries every telop and display word, a heavy rounded sans: Fredoka 700. Title 190 px with a 26 px ink stroke painted under the fill (`paint-order: stroke fill`, about 14 % of the size), letter-spacing 8 px, one span per glyph so each can pop; count-in numbers 340 px (36 px stroke); judgement word 120 px (18 px stroke); round-card name 104 px in ink; card time 56 px in `--utama-di-latar` with a 5 px stroke; tag pill 52 px (10 px stroke); banner time 64 px and name 54 px (12 px stroke); the subtitle under the title 60 px in `--teks`, letter-spacing 2 px; name tags 34 px white on the ink pill, scaled with the character.
- `--font-isi` carries the small black-weight lines: Poppins 800. Banner sub line 34 px, typed card lines 46 px.
- When the brand has no fonts: Fredoka 700 for display, Poppins 800 for lines; Archivo Black is a fair second for numbers. Avoid condensed faces (Bebas) and serifs: the look is round.
- Telops are the subtitles: keep a banner line within about 20 characters, a pill within 12, a judgement word to one or two words. A wider brand font gets more letter-spacing room, not a smaller size.

## 5. Motion quality

- **Grid**: 150 BPM, beat 0.4 s, bar 1.6 s. Scene changes on bar lines; events on beats; fast patterns on half and quarter beats.
- **Glyph pop**: each title glyph rises 120 px (`power3.out`) while scaling from 0 with `back.out(1.9)` in 0.3 s, 0.06 s apart; the subtitle 30 px, 0.25 s, 0.015 s apart, starting one beat later. From the fourth beat the title glyphs hop 12 px per beat, each 0.04 s behind the last.
- **Crowd drop**: each member falls 700 px in 0.3 s with a cubic ease-in and lands exactly on its slot time; back row on half beats, front row a quarter beat later, so one lands every 0.1 s (15 members in 1.5 s).
- **Landing squash**: scaleY = 1 − 0.3·e^(−14t)·cos(30t) for 0.35 s, scaleX = 1/√scaleY, pivot at the feet.
- **Idle**: a parabola hop per beat (26 px for the crowd, 10 px for a waiting contestant, 30 px for a winner), every other member half a beat later so the crowd ripples; a small squash (0.9) on each downbeat that recovers within a quarter beat. Arms out (88°) for the first 30 % of each beat, otherwise down (18°); mouth open for the first 20 %.
- **Shout**: arms up (158°), mouth open for the first half of each beat, happy closed eyes for a winner.
- **Count-in**: one number per beat for a bar (1-2-3-4), each pops to 1.15 in 0.12 s (`back.out`) and settles in 0.28 s, tilted −6° and +6° in turn; the title fades in 0.12 s on the first number and every character shouts.
- **Round card**: flies in from 1640 px right, rotation 8° to −2°, 0.25 s `back.out(1.9)`; pulses 1.03 → 1 on every beat (0.35 s `expo.out`); its icon hops 26 px per beat and sways ±6°; it leaves 2200 px left in the last 0.18 s (`power3.in`). Stripes scroll 300 px/s, rays turn 14°/s.
- **Banner**: slides in from 960 px left, −6° to −1.5°, 0.35 s `back.out(1.9)`.
- **Hit**: a contestant leaps 145 px in a parabola centred on the beat (±0.15 s) stretching to 1.16, mouth open from −0.12 to +0.05 s; the prop swings 7° in 0.08 s and settles with `elastic.out(1, 0.35)` over 0.5 s; a burst lives 0.3 s (scale 0.55 → 1.25, opacity 1 − p², a 30° spin). The final hit uses a burst 2.5× larger and a 4 % punch.
- **Judgement word**: pops in 0.25 s (`back.out(1.9)`) at −6°, drifts up 20 px over 0.6 s.
- **Typewriter**: one character per sixteenth of a beat (0.025 s).
- **Stamp**: appears 0.09 s before its beat at 2.6× and 30 % opacity, slams to 1× and 93 % with an ease-in, bounces to 1.05 and back in 0.12 s.
- **Cuts**: hard, on bar lines, with a white flash at 50 % fading in 0.08 s. A photo flash is 75 % over 0.16 s. Nothing fades in slowly; things are either on or popping.
- **Holds**: telop text at least 1.8 s; a judgement word may be read in 0.6 s; the ending holds 2 s or more, frozen.

## 6. Camera grammar

The stage is a frontal, symmetrical proscenium; the frame itself does the moving.

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Beat punch (zoom 1-4 % about the centre, decaying over 0.16 s, squared) | the hit, felt in the frame | a slam, a count-in, every bite or stamp |
| Several punches in one bar | the frame breathing with the pattern | an escalating round, a chorus of answers |
| Locked frontal wide | the whole stage as a game board | setting up a pattern, a crowd, a scoreboard |
| Hard cut on the bar line + white flash | a new round, a new set | chapter changes, a before/after |
| Shrink to thumbnail (a finished round scales to 25 % into a slot in 0.3 s) | memory, accumulation | a recap, the end card, "and all this happened" |
| Split stage (two halves, two sets) | two sides answering each other | a rivalry, old vs new, a quiz duel |
| Vertical scroll of the set | rising stakes or scale | a leaderboard, growth, a tower of items |
| Snap zoom onto one prop (cut to 2×, back on the next bar) | this detail is the joke | a price tag, a number, a face reacting |
| Freeze + photo flash | the moment is kept | the group photo ending, a winner's pose |

Keep the sum of overlapping punches below 0.06 so the frame edge never shows. Characters stand on the floor band; banners top-left, judgement words top-centre, round cards centre.

## 7. Native moves

- **Crowd drop and count-in.** The title pops glyph by glyph on a sunburst while the whole cast drops from the sky, one every tenth of a second with a name tag, then hops; a bar of 1-2-3-4 has everyone shouting. *Fits content like:* every stall at a night market; the members of a creator's community; the pupils of a new class; the cast of a short story introducing themselves.
- **Rounds with a card.** A one-bar card (round number on a pill, a name, a tag such as a time or a year, a hopping icon) flies in, then a hard cut with a flash to the play. *Fits content like:* the games of a neighbourhood festival; the steps of a recipe; the chapters of a course; the stages of a startup.
- **Call-and-response that speeds up.** Contestants take turns on the beat, then on half beats: the acceleration is the plot. *Fits content like:* three players biting crackers; a teacher's question and the class answer; a customer order and the barista's reply; two negotiators trading offers.
- **Judgement word.** A big outlined word pops at an angle on the round's last hit, with a big burst and the winner's arms up. *Fits content like:* "Mantap!" when a contestant finishes; "Terkirim!" on a delivery step; "Lulus!" on an exam; "Rekor baru!" on a training plan.
- **Shrink to thumbnail.** The finished round scales down into a slot on a card or along a timeline ribbon; at a climax all slots bounce together. *Fits content like:* the round we just played on a registration card; a year in review; a team's release list; a festival line-up.
- **Report card with a stamp.** Lines typed a sixteenth of a beat per character on a cream card, then a stamp slams from 2.6×. *Fits content like:* registration details stamped "GRATIS"; a quarterly review stamped "LULUS"; a trip summary; a final score.
- **Group photo.** Everyone freezes mid-hop with arms up under a white flash, and the frame holds. *Fits content like:* the end card of an event; a class graduating; a channel's subscriber milestone; the last page of a story.
- **Stats as game UI.** Numbers become podium scores, counters racing to a target, price tags hammered, bars growing one step per beat. *Fits content like:* donations collected for a mosque roof; calories per dish; downloads of an app; pages read in a reading challenge.

## 8. Pitfalls

- **Performance (live preview).** One `div` per character holding its own SVG, moved only by `transform` (compositor work); arm and mouth poses are SVG attribute changes, written only on the frames where the pose changes. Rays are one SVG drawn once and rotated; stripes are a gradient layer that translates and loops; dots are a static CSS pattern. No filters, blur or animated shadows.
- **Pure function of time.** Drive every hop, squash and punch from the timeline's time (a `render(t)` called from one tween's `onUpdate`), never from the previous frame: a render that seeks would show the wrong state.
- **Telop stroke.** The ink stroke must be painted under the fill (`paint-order: stroke fill`); a centred stroke on top eats thin letters. Split glyphs keep 8 px of letter-spacing so one glyph's stroke never covers its neighbour.
- **Hue clashes.** A character never stands on a set of its own hue; neighbouring rounds never share a hue.
- **Text before fonts.** Never measure text before the fonts load; estimate pill widths from the character count instead.
- **Clutter.** Name tags are decoration; keep the words that must be read (title, banner, judgement, card) few and big. At most one telop block and one card at a time.
- **Punch sum.** Overlapping punches add up; keep the total under 0.06.
- **Real brands as characters.** Names on tags and original mascots only, never logos, product UI or real people.

## 9. Variation space

You decide the rounds and their verbs, the cast, the sets, the opening and the ending. The grid, the drawing kit and the telop language stay.

- Structures: a tournament bracket (two contestants per round, the final as a split stage); one long round that escalates from quarters to sixteenths; a quiz show where each question is a fact and the scoreboard is the argument.
- Openings: the judgement first (a "Mantap!" on an empty stage, then rewind); one contestant alone hopping until the crowd drops in; a scoreboard counting back to zero.
- Endings: a group photo; a level map where every finished round is a lit node; a curtain falling bar by bar.

## 10. Measured from the reference

The 12-second reference: a sunburst title set from 0 to 6.4 s (title glyph pop at 0, subtitle on beat 1, the 15-member crowd dropping from 0.8 to 2.3 s, a 1-2-3-4 count-in on bar 3 from 4.8 s), the round card on bar 4 (6.4-8.0 s), the playing scene from 8.0 s with a corner banner and a move on every beat. Palette by share: sunburst yellow `#fdd85f` 42 %, orange set `#f1a15c` 39 %, ink and shadow `#72696c` 13 %, cream `#e3d7cc` 6 %. Motion energy is steady (hops never stop); the only cuts are on bar lines.

# Game show: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.6, medium 3.2, long 4.8.

## hook

- en: a sunburst set: the title pops glyph by glyph, the cast drops from the sky one per 0.1 s, then a 1-2-3-4 count-in
- id: set sinar matahari: judul meletup per huruf, para pemeran jatuh dari langit satu per satu, lalu hitungan 1-2-3-4

## problem

- en: a contestant misses on the beat: X eyes, a sweat drop and a buzzer cross pop, the frame punches
- id: peserta meleset di ketukan: mata silang, keringat menetes, tanda silang merah meletup, layar terhentak

## fact

- en: a corner banner slides in (time, name, one line) over a new set while the cast keeps hopping on the beat
- id: papan nama sudut meluncur masuk (jam, nama, satu baris) di set baru, para pemeran tetap loncat di ketukan

## step

- en: a round card flies in for one bar, then a hard cut and flash to the play: one verb repeated on every beat
- id: kartu babak masuk satu birama, lalu potong keras dan kilat ke permainan: satu gerakan diulang tiap ketukan

## compare

- en: split stage, two sets: the sides answer each other on alternate beats; the winning side gets the judgement word
- id: panggung dibelah dua set: kedua sisi saling jawab di ketukan bergantian; sisi pemenang dapat kata penilaian

## number

- en: stats as game UI: a podium score climbs one step per beat to the target, the last hit stamps the figure
- id: angka jadi skor permainan: skor podium naik tiap ketukan sampai target, pukulan terakhir mengecap angkanya

## proof

- en: call and response speeds up from beats to half beats; on the last hit a big outlined word pops at an angle
- id: saling sahut makin cepat, dari tiap ketukan ke tiap setengah ketukan; di pukulan terakhir kata besar meletup miring

## offer

- en: a price tag drops on the beat and is hammered; a stamp slams onto it from 2.6x
- id: label harga jatuh tepat di ketukan lalu dipalu; cap menghantam dari ukuran 2,6x

## cta

- en: the round shrinks into a slot on a cream card; contact typed, a stamp slams, the cast freezes for a photo, held 2 s
- id: babak mengecil ke slot kartu krem; kontak diketik, cap menghantam, pemeran beku untuk foto bersama, diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: a report card typed line by line with a grade stamp; everyone freezes mid-hop under a white flash, held 2 s
- id: rapor diketik baris demi baris dengan cap nilai; semua beku di udara saat kilat putih, diam 2 detik
